#3750. Remember PS5-exclusive shooter Fairgame$? It’s reportedly canceled now, to no one’s surprise

Well, it seems like this one was only a matter of time.

Sony has reportedly canceled the long-missing online shooter Fairgame$ after it went missing in the public eye for years, according to Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier, adding to a long list of canceled PlayStation projects this generation.

Schreier said that “a recent test of the game with thousands of players did not deliver on the results PlayStation expected,” according to an internal email sent to employees today.

First revealed at PlayStation Showcase way back in May 2023, the game seemed to be themed around online heist PvP gameplay. But it hasn’t been seen since, and this cancellation comes as little surprise, as rumors about turmoil in development have been swirling for some time.

“While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” executives Sean Decker and John Doyle said in the memo. “Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.”

Earlier this year, it was reported that Fairgame$ was pivoting away from the “heist” mechanic and instead focusing on the extraction game type, similar to Bungie’s Marathon and Call of Duty’s DMZ. It apparently did not work out.

Fairgame$, developed by Haven Studios, joins a long list of PS5 projects that did not make the cut this generation as Sony incessantly chased live-service success. Concord launched and was quickly shuttered, while The Last of Us Factions, a God of War game, a Spider-Man game, Twisted Metal, and more never saw the light of day from PS5’s games-as-a-service initiative.

According to Schreier, “there will be no job cuts as a result of the cancellation,” and “Haven will instead move to support other studios within the organization.”

More than a year after its initial release, physical versions of Hollow Knight: Silksong are finally arriving on players' doorsteps. It's the same brilliant and sometimes thrillingly cruel Metroidvania Eurogamer gave five stars to, except this time a pack-in booklet seemingly reveals the existence of multiple "free content packs" alongside the Sea of Sorrow DLC.

Hollow Knight: Silksong's physical editions were originally set to be delivered from 10th November, but some early handovers have given us a peek inside the box. Redditor Me_975 posted pictures of their Nintendo Switch 2 Edition, and there's a few interesting tidbits tucked away - most notably in the manual's chapter on Content Packs.

"The world of Hollow Knight: Silksong will expand with free content packs," the booklet reads. "Prepare for even more adventures filled with new friends, new abilities, and new ferocious foes!"

Developer Team Cherry confirmed plans for post-launch Silksong support last year, but remained pretty tight-lipped about what exactly that would look like. The indie outfit then announced the nautically themed Sea of Sorrow expansion, though we now have proper confirmation there's more content packs still to come, which shouldn't be a huge shocker considering all the free post-launch love Hollow Knight (the first one) received.

Speaking of Sea of Sorrow, that's mentioned here too: "In the first giant expansion, voyage across and beneath a salt-stricken ocean brimming with mystery and menace."

Sea of Sorrow's original release window was a vague 2026 - time's a-ticking, Team Cherry. Still no release date so far, but the booklet does say it's "Coming Soon." Of course, Team Cherry are quite infamous for working on games until they balloon wildly out of control. If you are interested in owning Silksong physically, it comes with a big map of Pharloom and the rest of the booklet also includes some really lovely art seemingly ripped straight from the game, as well.

The Primals' Eikichi Iwai has died at the age of 57.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Final Fantasy 14 players have been gathering en masse across servers today in the wake of the news that Eikichi Iwai—the bassist behind the game's band The Primals—has passed away at the age of 57.

A post went out on The Lodestone in the early hours of this morning (November 11) which read: "Thank you very much for your continued support of The Primals. As announced earlier today, we are deeply saddened to share the news of the sudden passing of bassist Eikichi Iwai.

"Having witnessed his truly unforgettable performance on stage at the recent Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival in Japan, the sudden news of his passing has come as a profound shock. The members of The Primals and the entire FF14 Development and Operations teams are overcome with deep sorrow.

"As we reflect on all that Eikichi-san has left behind, our thoughts are with him, and we offer our heartfelt condolences."

The Primals is Final Fantasy 14's in-house band, fronted by composer Masayoshi Soken and localisation lead Michael-Christopher Koji Fox, and accompanied by Tetsuya Tachibana, GUNN, and Iwai himself.

Iwai's bass in particular has elevated a ton of already-excellent tracks across the game's history: Stormblood's Amatsu Kaze, Shadowbringers' To the Edge, Endwalker's Scream and Close in the Distance, and Dawntrail's Ride the Rhythm just to name a few. The Primals has just come off the back of a strong year for live performances, too—from their usual appearance at all three Fan Festivals that took place this year, to even taking the stage at the UK's biggest rock and music festival as part of Download's lineup.

A quick trip through some of Final Fantasy 14's European servers have seen tons of players gathering in main hubs like Limsa Lominsa to pay their respects and share what it is about Iwai's work that meant so much to them. As I write this story, players and campfires line the perimeter of Omega's Limsa Lominsa plaza—a common practice for honouring the passing of key community figures and beyond, something which I've previously witnessed for the likes of Berserk's creator Kentaro Miura and Dragon Ball creator Akira Toriyama.

It's a small gesture, but one which is a pleasant reminder of why Final Fantasy 14 continues to maintain such an iron grip on myself and many others.

#3747. How to gain more Followers in Warhammer Survivors

Gaining Followers in Warhammer Survivors has many benefits when it comes to the survival aspect of the game. Not only do they help you survive and last longer in the battle, but you’ll need to gain a minimum number if you want to complete the objectives.

While this method talks about gaining 5 followers, it can be any arbitrary number. I say 5 because that’s a requirement of an in-game objective that unlocks a crucial item. There is more than one way to gain followers, but this will be the easiest one for you.

First, unlock Trooper Bartosz Kozlowski and Sister Superior Amalia Novena, followed by their respective weapons. Now, begin a fresh run with Malum Caedo.

Once you’re deeper into your run, you’ll be offered the Lasgun and Shield of Faith as available weapons. Grab both of them, and then upgrade the Lasgun to Level 6. This will make Bartosz Kozlowski bring the required number of followers.

If you’re one short, that’s where Sister Amalia comes in. Once you acquire the Shield of Faith as a weapon, you’ll manage to have her as a companion. This will also unlock the Figure Case passive skill that allows you to return after dying.

You can repeat the same process with other characters in the game. Several characters allow you to add to the count of Followers when you unlock their signature weapon and level it up. However, the characters I have mentioned above are easy to unlock, and they will allow you to get to five Followers fast.

Does complimenting a waiter make you a terrible husband?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Kristen Bell is back on the 2026 TV schedule thanks to Netflix's Nobody Wants This, but lately, her marriage to Dax Shepard seems to be generating just as many headlines as her career. The couple has never been particularly shy about sharing the stranger details of their relationship. We've heard about naked yoga, some rather disgusting behind-the-scenes favors and a number of other personal anecdotes. But Shepard has apparently had enough of strangers picking apart their marriage, especially when those conversations turn into accusations about how he treats his wife.

During the Nov. 9 "Fact Check" portion of his Armchair Expert podcast, which followed an interview with Rhea Seehorn, the Parenthood actor addressed renewed speculation about his marriage. He generally ignores criticism, but recent headlines reached Bell:

Another round of me being a terrible person was in the media, and like I avoided that, but then it hit Kristen’s doorstep really hard, and then I got to find out everything people were saying about me, and I think I was just at that moment where I was at like, ‘The level of injustice it feels to me, my behavior vs this weird narrative that is surrounding me, like I’m controlling, abusive, and I’m now flirting with people in public which I don't do…

The latest controversy started with something Bell said during an October appearance on her husband's podcast. The Nobody Wants This star explained that she enjoys watching Shepard compliment strangers, including restaurant servers. She said that was his way of flirting with her.

That description spread online, with some commenters interpreting it as Shepard openly flirting with others. Another group of people connected it to previous stories the couple had shared and alleged that he behaved that way at home. Shepard denied those accusations and clarified that he was often complimenting men, not pursuing waitresses.

Interestingly, Bell previously said Bruce Willis inspired Shepard's habit of generously tipping service workers. She even described his generosity as one of her favorite things about him. So, this whole business about complimenting waiters isn't exactly coming out of nowhere.

I can see why the original anecdote raised eyebrows, but that's a pretty dramatic journey from complimenting somebody's eyelashes to passing judgment on a couple's entire marriage. Shepard was especially frustrated that the discussion had spilled over from internet speculation into what he called mainstream coverage. He continued:

Pretty big, normal publications, running this … for me, growing up around certain men who behaved a certain way, and then literally dedicating my whole life to being the opposite of all that… I don’t ever yell at my children, I don’t swear at them, I don’t yell at my wife… to have given it my all to be the opposite of what now, some group of people are saying I am, is, its hard…. I don’t love it. And I find it deeply insulting to my wife, additionally.

Those are serious allegations, and Shepard's comments are his account of his behavior, of course. But it's also understandable that he'd want to address them, especially given what he says about growing up around men whose behavior he never wanted to repeat. He went further, arguing that the accusations make a pretty unflattering assumption about Bell herself:

Like what, she’s sitting in her house with her two daughters and modeling some abusive relationship? It's very offensive to her.

Of course, this is hardly the first time the couple has found themselves at the center of an internet argument. Earlier this year, Bell's Nobody Wants This co-star and others defended the couple. Their marriage also received criticism over Bell's controversial anniversary joke involving domestic violence.

And while I can understand people having opinions about things celebrities choose to share publicly, I don't think we can know everything happening in someone's marriage from a podcast anecdote. Shepard also discussed growing up around abusive men and said he'd spent much of his life trying to avoid repeating their behavior. Hearing himself described that way was understandably difficult, according to the actor.

Bell and Shepard have been married since 2013, and they've previously discussed what they appreciate about their relationship. I imagine they'll continue sharing their sometimes wonderfully bizarre stories. But judging by Shepard's latest comments, he's getting pretty tired of people treating every new anecdote as an invitation to investigate his marriage.

Personally, I don't need every celebrity couple to share their dinner-table conversations with me. But I also don't think a single podcast story gives strangers enough information to diagnose a marriage. If anything, Shepard clearly wishes this particular one had stayed a story about a compliment.

#3745. God of War: Ragnarok is reportedly the highest-earning PlayStation Studios game this generation, but Marvel's Spider-Man 2 isn't far behind

God of War: Ragnarok is the generation's best-selling and highest-earning PlayStation Studios game, according to a new report, but the full top 10 list has a few nice surprises.

In the four years since its PS5 release and two years since its PC port, God of War: Ragnarok has reportedly sold just over 20m copies and generated $1.4b in revenue, according to estimates from Alinea Analytics. About 27.5 percent of the 15m copies it sold on console came from physical editions, and the action blockbuster apparently sold a further 1.1m this year alone. Not bad, boy.

Those stats should bode well for the series' next romp God of War: Laufey - which sees Faye take the spotlight across a multi-mythological afterlife and was recently delayed into May 2027 - even if PlayStation moves away from PC ports for its signature single-player games.

Kratos and Atreus only narrowly beat out perhaps the biggest superhero of them all: Marvel's Spider-Man 2, a game that reportedly made a whopping $1.3b off 19.1m copies across PS5 and PC. The Spidey sequel should keep swinging even higher as the years chug on, though - the report states that sales always surge during the holiday months, and this year's big screen behemoth Spider-Man: Brand New Day led to an even bigger spike than usual.

Racing sim royalty Gran Turismo 7 ($841m), bug-squashing phenomenon Helldivers 2 ($786m), robo-dino sequel Horizon: Forbidden West ($485m), vengeful spirit sim Ghost of Yotei ($410m), undead remake The Last of Us Part 1 ($341m), multidimensional romp Ratchet and Clank: Rift Apart ($334m), Stellar Blade ($316m) and delightful throwback Astro Bot ($292m) round out the top 10 games published by PlayStation Studios this generation.

It's worth noting that Helldivers 2 and Stellar Blade were developed by studios outside the PlayStation umbrella, but the console maker still published both upon release. Ghost of Yotei's performance is also particularly impressive since Sucker Punch's sequel has only been out for a year and didn't get the benefit of a PC port, like many of its PS5 siblings. The success couldn't save Sucker Punch from recent layoffs, however.

On PlayStation's decision to kill disc-based physical releases, analyst Rhys Elliott said that the bottom five games in the list together made $281.7m this year alone: "PlayStation wants those numbers to be bigger in the coming years, which is one of the reasons it's killing the disc (alongside the better margins it and publishers get through digital.)"

#3744. How to get the crude lockpick recipe in DREADMOOR, all lockpick types, and how to use them

Although brute force can take you far in DREADMOOR, having a lockpick at hand is a requirement if you wish to get past locked doors and access treasure chests across the game’s many settlements.

But getting the tool means first acquiring its recipe, something only doable a few hours in. Here’s how to get the first lockpick recipe in DREADMOOR and how the mechanic works.

You can unlock the Crude Lockpick recipe in DREADMOOR as a reward by completing the Catch a Mutant Fish Story Quest. The quest is unlocked after meeting Mad Nick on his island and requires catching two Cryptmaw fish.

The fish can be found in the locations below, but only late at night. You will also need to have at least 30 Line Strength to attempt the catch, so don’t forget to equip the Braided Line to your fishing rod at the trading post to meet the requirements.

After returning to Mad Nick and unlocking the recipe, you will be able to craft the Crude Lockpick by using 1x Rubber and 1x Metal Plate. You can have a maximum of twelve in your inventory. Just don’t forget, they will share slots with First Aid Kits.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

You can pick locks in DREADMOOR by first using your mouse to position your lockpick and find the sweet spot within the lock, marked by a glowing light. Now, hold D to turn the lock while keeping the tool in the right position to unlock it. Forcing the lock will cause your lockpick to break.

Apart from the Crude Lockpick, you can unlock two other variants in DREADMOOR: the standard iron Lockpick and the Master Lockpick. Both are clear upgrades and can be crafted after unlocking their respective recipes.

We will be adding more to the above once we unlock the recipes for the advanced lockpicks. In the meantime, don’t forget to check out all Fishing Rods and how they work in DREADMOOR.
